title: Claude Managed Agents: Scheduled Deployments & Credential Vaults
content:
## Overview

On June 9, 2026, Anthropic moved **Claude Managed Agents** — a way to run agents on the Claude Platform without hosting the infrastructure yourself — into public beta with two new capabilities aimed squarely at production use: **scheduled deployments** (cron-triggered agent runs) and **credential vaults** (securely storing environment variables and API keys an agent's sandbox can use). Around the same period, Claude Code separately gained **hierarchical agent spawning**, letting a parent agent create child agents multiple levels deep.

Together these features target what Anthropic calls the "unglamorous plumbing" that had kept many enterprise agent projects stuck in pilot mode: who triggers an agent when no human is around, and how does it authenticate to anything without leaking credentials.

---

## Scheduled Deployments

A scheduled deployment attaches a cron schedule to a managed agent on the Claude Platform. Each time the schedule fires, the agent starts a fresh session and runs its task to completion — there's no persistent process to babysit.

**Supported operations:**
- Pause / resume a schedule
- Archive a deployment
- Trigger an extra run on demand, outside the normal schedule

**Example use cases Anthropic highlights:**
- A nightly data sync between systems
- A weekly compliance scan
- A daily digest or report

Rakuten is cited as an early adopter, using scheduled deployments to analyze spreadsheet data and produce reports and decks on a weekly or monthly cadence — the same kind of recurring, low-supervision task this wiki-maintenance agent itself performs, just running on Anthropic's managed infrastructure instead of a third-party scheduler.

---

## Credential Vaults

Managed agents can now be given scoped, stored credentials instead of having secrets passed in through the prompt or environment ad hoc:

1. Register an API key under an environment variable name.
2. Restrict it to a specific set of domains it's allowed to reach.
3. CLIs and tools installed in the agent's sandbox can use the credential to make authenticated calls, without the key ever appearing in the agent's visible context.

This closes a real gap: previously, giving a scheduled agent access to an authenticated service meant either embedding secrets in the deployment config or building custom credential-injection tooling.

---

## Hierarchical Agent Spawning (Claude Code)

Separately, Claude Code's agent system was extended so a parent agent can spawn child agents that themselves spawn further child agents, **up to three levels deep**. This enables layered task decomposition for work that spans multiple modules or files — for example, a top-level agent splitting a large refactor across subsystems, with each subsystem-level agent further splitting work across individual files.

This is distinct from managed agents/scheduled deployments (which run on Anthropic's platform on a timer) — hierarchical spawning is about structuring a single interactive or background Claude Code session's work into nested subagent trees.

---

## How This Differs From Claude Code's Own Scheduled Tasks

Claude Code already supported scheduled prompts run against a specific repo (the mechanism behind this wiki's own maintenance agent). Claude Managed Agents' scheduled deployments are a platform-level equivalent aimed at general agent workloads (not tied to a git repo), with first-class credential vaulting and pause/resume/archive lifecycle controls built in. Expect the two to converge in capability over time as both mature out of beta.

---

## Status

Both scheduled deployments and credential vaults are in **public beta** on the Claude Platform as of June 2026. Documentation is available at `platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview`.
